header: Sub CPU: enemy movement, formation and sprite bookkeeping. It shares
$0000-$1FFF with the main CPU but has no access to sound or I/O. Its
foreground runs the same kind of per-mode task lists as the main CPU
(game_mode $102F, task index $107A); its IRQ copies its sprites into
sprite RAM and meets the main CPU's IRQ at frame_sync ($10AF).

E000.name: reset_sub
doc: Sub CPU reset (released by the main CPU's SRESET_OFF write).
DP = $10, S = $1D80; wait for $11 in $0800 from the main CPU;
checksum $A000-$BFFF, $C000-$DFFF, $E000-$FFFF (byte sums must be
0; failures leave '6', '5', '4' in $0801, shown by the service
mode); answer $22 in $0800; 256 times write $6001 (IRQ on) and
$500F (unmapped in MAME; meaning unknown); enable interrupts and
enter the task scheduler.

E061.name: irq_sub
doc: Sub CPU vblank IRQ.
- acknowledge (even VINTON address = IRQ off);
- copy the sub's sprites from the shadow buffers ($0E00-$0EE1 +
banks $1600/$1E00; bit 7 of the flag byte = in use) into sprite
RAM from slot 1 ($0F82) up to slot 39, mirrored when the screen
is flipped; unused slots get Y/flags $F000 (parked off-screen);
- frame_sync = $11 and wait for the main CPU's IRQ to answer $22
(the two IRQ handlers meet here every frame);
- IRQ on (odd VINTON address), RTI.

E0EC.name: task_dispatch_sub
doc: The sub CPU's scheduler: jump through
sub_mode_task_lists[game_mode][sub_task]. Tasks end with
INC <$7A / JMP task_dispatch_sub; the last one
(task_end_frame_sub) waits for the IRQ and restarts the list.

E0F9.name: sub_mode_task_lists
doc: One task list per game mode 0-9 (pointers).

E13F.name: sub_tasks_mode5
doc: Mode 5: normal play (the longest list).

E16B.name: sub_tasks_mode6
doc: Mode 6: stage clear.

E171.name: sub_tasks_mode7
doc: Mode 7: challenging stage.

E17F.name: task_end_frame_sub
doc: Last task of every list: CWAI for the next IRQ, reset the stack,
restart the list.

E18A.name: task_stage_setup
doc: Mode 2 task: build the stage's enemy sprites and formation state
from the stage tables (index $106E), then game_mode + 1.

BF58.name: task_formation_init
doc: Mode 0 task: mark all 44 formation slots occupied and load the
formation pointers.

B90E.name: task_animate_objects
doc: Run the state machines of the four objects in $111D-$1120
(sprites $0EE2, $0EEC, $0EF6, $0F00) through object_states.

B936.name: object_spawn_random
doc: State 1: place the object at a pseudo-random position. The sub has
no random number generator: Y is the byte of its own reset code
at $E000 + frame_counter (the ROM used as a noise table, clamped
to $20-$CF: below $20 -> $90, $D0 and up -> $60), and X is
frame_counter | $B0.

BFEF.name: checksum_A000
doc: Checksum adjust: the byte sum of $A000-$BFFF is 0 (tested at
boot or in the service mode).

DFEF.name: checksum_C000
doc: Checksum adjust: the byte sum of $C000-$DFFF is 0 (tested at
boot or in the service mode).

FFEF.name: checksum_E000
doc: Checksum adjust: the byte sum of $E000-$FFFF is 0 (tested at
boot or in the service mode).

comments.E0E2: wait for the main CPU's IRQ
